question: Why can a high-capacity model sometimes fit randomized labels, and what does that tell us?
direct_answer: Because it has enough flexibility to store arbitrary mappings, showing that low training loss alone does not imply meaningful learning.
expanded_answer: If a model is expressive enough, it can match even labels with no real relationship to the inputs. That means the training objective can be minimized without discovering a useful pattern. This is an important warning: a good fit on the training set may reflect memorization capacity rather than extraction of structure that will transfer to new data.
key_points: Random labels remove real predictive structure
Low loss can be achieved without meaningful learning
Generalization requires more than interpolation of the training set
common_wrong_ideas: Assuming any fit must reflect true pattern discovery
Believing model size alone guarantees better generalization
